subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: CONFORMS, unchanged in substance and re-homed by kb/Work PB802. The rule - 'The data description of data-name-1 or data-name-2 as well as their relative location within a record shall be the same as that used when the file was created' (note: 'the file', not 'the physical file'; 12.4.5.6.4 GR3 is the one worded 'the physical file', and the inherited quotation that gave both the same wording is corrected here) - states a requirement and no consequence where it is written; 14.9.27.4 GR10's file attribute conflict condition is the mechanism that detects a violation. WHAT CHANGED: the prime key's descriptor is no longer written into a .cbattr catalog sidecar beside the data file but into the framed store's own HEADER, which RecordFraming.WriteStore stamps from the writing connector's DeclaredAttributes on every persist - so the file itself carries its key geometry, as a real ISAM file does, and nothing exists beside it that could outlive it. FixedFileAttributes.Conflicts compares it on every later OPEN and a mismatch is the unsuccessful OPEN with I-O status '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7). THE RECORDED DESCRIPTOR IS THE KEY'S WINDOW PLUS ITS COLLATING SEQUENCE, and that is the whole of 'the data description ... as well as their relative location' this implementation can act on: 12.4.5.12.3 SR2 confines a record key to category alphanumeric or category national, 12.4.5.12.4 GR1 makes key equality a relation condition under the file's collating sequence (recorded by weights - FixedFileAttributes.Fingerprint), and both native sequences are one code-unit ordinal over the UTF-16 substrate (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-33 / DOC-A.1-188), so two descriptions sharing a window and a sequence order every key value identically whatever their category. NEW: the comparison of the key table alone can be turned off for a run by WISEOWL_COBOL_KEYCHECK=OFF, GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK opt-out under this repository's naming, documented as part of the A.1 item 129 determination (DOC-A.1-129) - by default it is on, so the rule is enforced unless a run explicitly asks otherwise. Pinned by open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix step I2 (a six-byte prime key window over a file created with a four-byte one gives '39') and by the unit theory's prime-window arm. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/RecordFraming.cs#WriteStore (kb/Work PB2660 split the store write into ComposeStore (the framing) and KeyedConnector.Persist (the positional I/O); WriteStore no longer exists) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/RecordFraming.cs#ComposeStore (the whole-store model's remains are deleted (kb/Work PB3335; DESIGN-runtime-library 2.2.1.13): the key's fixed attributes are recorded by the one key codec of the meta page (MetaPage.WriteKeyDescriptor), not by a whole store's header)
